# Extra dynamic control-flow edges for apple2tc's --code-at.
#
# Format: "ORIGIN TARGET", hexadecimal, '$' optional, '#' starts a comment.
# Each line asserts that the branch at ORIGIN can transfer control to TARGET.
#
# These edges are *asserted by hand*, not observed. That is exactly why they
# live here and not in neptune.json: the JSON is a recording of what actually
# happened during a play session, and editing it to claim reachability the run
# never saw would destroy its value as evidence. Every line below must carry
# the argument for why the edge is real.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# $0000 -> $0100: the b33's entry trampoline.
#
# neptune.b33 is entered at its load address, which the .b33 loader forces to
# be the lowest byte in the file, so the entry is $0000 and the three bytes
# there are `JMP $0100`. The stub at $0100 restores those three bytes, sets the
# soft switches and the registers, and jumps to $3523. See scripts/make-b33.sh.
#
# The edge is not observed for a mechanical reason rather than an interesting
# one: --collect starts recording at the moment the b33 is loaded, and the
# recorded BranchTargets contain nothing below $0200, so the $0000 -> $0100
# transfer is absent from the run data. The block at $0100 is therefore
# disassembled -- it is in the listing, and in the generated C -- but it never
# becomes a *dynamic* block, so the generated address-to-block map has no entry
# for it and the c1 build stops at once with `Unknown address $0100`.
#
# This is as certain as an asserted edge gets. The three bytes at $0000 are
# `4C 00 01`, this file generated them, and both the interpreter and the
# --simple-c build execute the transfer on every run.
0000 0100

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# $36B0: the paddle reader, code only because the game writes a call to it.
#
# A root rather than an edge, because there is no branch to attach an edge to.
# poll_input_select_mode at $3584 chooses the input device once, at the title
# screen, and then rewrites three sites. Its joystick arm, $3700, is a pure
# constant patcher: it stores
#
#   $1060: 20 B0 36 4C 80 11   JSR $36B0 / JMP $1180
#   $1300: AD 61 C0 30 07 60   LDA PB0 / BMI $130C / RTS
#   $138C: AD 62 C0 30 05 60   LDA PB1 / BMI $1396 / RTS
#
# so `JSR $36B0` exists only as three bytes in $3700's operand stream. In the
# captured image $1060 holds the keyboard arm's `LDA $C000`, which is not a
# branch, so --code-at rejected the edge form here.
#
# The bytes decode cleanly as a textbook paddle read and nothing else fits:
# INC $A1 / LDA PTRIG / LDY #$90 / (LDA PADDL0,X : BPL out : DEY : BNE) with
# X = $A1 & 1, so one axis per call, alternating. The remaining count is then
# banded by CPY #$10 and CPY #$30 into -1 / 0 / +1 stored to $E3 (paddle 1) or
# $E4 (paddle 0). $3040 swaps the two immediates at $36CD and $36DB, which is
# an axis inversion, and is why the listing warns that those bytes are
# modified.
#
# This is an assertion about untraced bytes and cannot be checked by the gate:
# no scenario here selects joystick mode, because holding a button is not yet
# expressible in a headless replay. What can be said is that the region is not
# reached as data either -- no generation in neptune.json writes $36B0-$36F5,
# and the coverage report does not claim it.
36B0
